text:
Kai: heads-up — saw a flurry of node-exporter restarts in us-west-2 starting ~06:12 UTC, caused spike in alert noise
Maria: ah, saw that too. pods bounce every ~30s on a subset of nodes, looks like readiness probe failing after exporter upgrade
Devon: exporter logs show OOM killed while scraping /proc for per-cgroup metrics — memory growth when many short-lived containers present
Sasha: could be the new textfile/collector change that keeps all cgroup labels in memory; cardinality ballooned
Kai: possibility: custom runtime exporter (redwood_runtime_metrics) is also emitting per-request labels (request_id) — adds tons of unique series to Prom
Maria: we should throttle restarts and limit cardinality ASAP. Options: 1) roll back node-exporter 2) patch prometheus relabeling to drop high-cardinality labels 3) change DaemonSet flags to disable the offending collectors
Devon: agree. short-term -> drop request_id and span_id at scrape level, long-term -> release fixed exporter image that avoids storing ephemeral label maps
Sasha: proposed quick patch to Prometheus scrape config (metric_relabel_configs):
```yaml
- job_name: 'node-exporter'
  static_configs:
  - targets: ['<nodes>']
  metric_relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: ['request_id','span_id']
    action: 'labeldrop'
  - regex: '.*container_.*'
    action: 'labeldrop'
```
Maria: also add recording rule to collapse high-cardinality gauge to summarized per-node value to reduce series churn:
```yaml
- record: node:runtime_errors:sum
  expr: sum by (instance) (rate(redwood_runtime_errors_total[5m]))
```
Kai: operational change: set DaemonSet updateStrategy to OnDelete and canary one node first. Patch we can run: `kubectl -n monitoring patch daemonset node-exporter -p '{"spec":{"updateStrategy":{"type":"OnDelete"}}}'`
Sasha: will schedule canary on infra-canary-03 and watch Prom scrape target count and TSDB head memory for 20m
prometheus-bot: alert: HighSeriesCardinality firing (P3) — head_series increased 3.8x in last 15m
infra-bot: started incident channel #incidents/generic-metrics-cardinality and added runbook link https://go/redwood/runbooks/metrics-cardinality
Devon: for cost control, also enable relabel to drop top-level pod_name label for runtime metrics; that's causing remote_write to bill us heavily
Maria: agreed. And throttle restarts: increase liveness probe failure threshold to avoid cascade during transient memory spikes:
```yaml
livenessProbe:
  httpGet: { path: "/metrics", port: 9100 }
  initialDelaySeconds: 20
  periodSeconds: 10
  failureThreshold: 10
```
Kai: plan: 1) apply metric_relabel_configs (scrape-level) 2) patch daemonset updateStrategy -> OnDelete 3) canary restart single node-exporter 4) if stable -> rollout rest of nodes with OnDelete + manual pod delete in batches 5) prepare backout to previous image if OOMs persist
Sasha: I'll own the patch and canary tonight at 02:00 PDT, will post telemetry (head_series, tsdb_head_chunk_count, node-exporter OOMs)
Maria: I'll update alerting: mute HighSeriesCardinality for 2h and create temporary suppression for flapping node-exporter restarts to avoid pager fatigue
Devon: reminder — follow up ticket to add exporter config flag to disable per-cgroup collector and to sanitize labels at source (avoid sending request_id/span_id). Also add e2e test for cardinality regression
Kai: thanks. if we need rollback, tag for rollback will be `node-exporter:v1.5.2-rollback` and we can use the imagePullPolicy trick to avoid re-pulling new image
Maria: noted. posting runbook steps in #incidents and will update on progress
Sasha: canary done — node infra-canary-03 stable for 25m, head_series dropped ~68%, no further OOMs observed
prometheus-bot: recovered: HighSeriesCardinality resolved
Kai: nice work. follow-up actions: schedule a maintenance window for full rollout, add recording rules to prevent similar spikes, and include cardinality checks in our CI for exporter changes
Maria: closing loop — will file RFC for exporter label hygiene and include cost estimates for remote_write impact
Devon: closing — thanks team :thumbsup:
